exercises.name: Triceps Extension (Suspension)

source_english.description: Triceps Extension (Suspension) faces away from anchored straps and bends the elbows to lower the forehead before pressing away.
instructions: Stand facing away from straps anchored overhead, lean forward with arms extended and body straight.
Grip the suspension handles with palms facing down and keep the upper arms fixed beside or above the torso.
Bend the elbows to lower the resistance to the forehead or behind the head.
Pause at the endpoint, then extend the elbows to return to straight arms.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load you can lower slowly and keep clear space around the head.

exercises.name: Wide Pull Up

source_english.description: Wide Pull Up uses an overhand grip wider than shoulder width to pull the body toward a fixed bar.
instructions: Grip the pull-up bar overhand with hands wider than shoulder width and start from a controlled hang.
Brace the trunk and pull the elbows down and out until the chin reaches bar height.
Pause without craning the neck.
Lower until the elbows are straight and reset.
source_english.safety_note: Use assistance or a shorter range until the wide grip remains controlled.

exercises.name: Box Squat (Barbell)

source_english.description: Box Squat (Barbell) bends the hips and knees through a box-targeted squat path before returning to standing.
instructions: Stand with the barbell across the upper back and place a box behind the hips.

Pause on the box while keeping the torso braced.
Drive through the feet to stand without bouncing.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a depth and load that keep the feet, knees, and spine stable.

exercises.name: Gorilla Row (Kettlebell)

source_english.description: Gorilla Row (Kettlebell) uses two kettlebells from a wide hip hinge, alternating close-elbow pulls toward the ribs.
instructions: Stand in a wide stance holding one kettlebell in each hand.
Hinge forward until the torso is inclined and keep the spine long.
Row the right kettlebell toward the right ribs while the left arm stays long.
Lower it, row the left kettlebell, and continue alternating without twisting the hips.
source_english.safety_note: Use kettlebells you can control from the wide hinged stance and stop if the back loses position.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Around the World

source_english.description: The kettlebell around the world passes the bell in a continuous circle around the waist while the feet stay planted.
instructions: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the kettlebell in front of the body.
Pass it from one hand around the side of the waist to the other hand behind the back.
Continue the circle around the torso while keeping the trunk upright and the feet planted.
Reverse direction for balanced repetitions, then return the bell to the front.
form_cues: Keep the circle close to the waist.
Brace the abdomen and keep the shoulders relaxed.
common_mistakes: Swinging the bell away from the body.
Twisting the knees and feet instead of the trunk.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light kettlebell and keep fingers clear during each handoff.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Curl

source_english.description: A kettlebell curl flexes the elbow to bring the bell toward the shoulder while the upper arm stays beside the torso.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold the kettlebell with the palm facing forward.
Keep the upper arm close to the torso and brace the trunk.
Curl the kettlebell toward the shoulder without swinging the body.
Squeeze the biceps briefly, then lower the bell until the elbow is straight.
form_cues: Keep the elbow under the shoulder.
Lower through the full controlled range.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to lift the bell.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light load if the kettlebell pulls the wrist out of alignment.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat

source_english.description: Hold one kettlebell at the chest while sitting the hips down and standing through both feet.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell close to your chest with both hands.
Keeping your chest up and core engaged, lower your body down into a squat position by bending at the knees and hips.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as you can comfortably go.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Track the knees with the toes.
Keep the chest and trunk controlled.
source_english.safety_note: Use a depth and load that allow a stable knee and hip path.

exercises.name: Landmine Row

source_english.description: A landmine row pulls the anchored barbell toward the ribs from a braced hip hinge.
instructions: Load the free end of the anchored barbell and stand over it with a hip-width stance.
Hinge forward with a neutral back and grasp the sleeve or handle with both hands.
Pull the bar toward the lower ribs while keeping the hips and torso steady.
Pause, then lower the bar until the arms are long without rounding the back.
form_cues: Brace the abdomen before each pull.
Let the shoulder blades move naturally at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Standing upright to finish each row.
Shrugging instead of pulling the elbows back.
source_english.safety_note: Ensure the landmine base is secure and keep the free end clear of your feet.

exercises.name: Lateral Box Jump

source_english.description: A lateral box jump uses a two-foot sideways takeoff and a quiet landing on a stable box.
instructions: Stand beside a stable box with feet about hip-width apart and knees softly bent.
Dip at the hips and knees, then drive sideways and upward with both legs.
Land quietly on top of the box with both feet and knees aligned.
Stand tall, step down carefully, and reset before the next jump.
form_cues: Use a box height you can clear comfortably.
common_mistakes: Jumping before checking the box is stable.
source_english.safety_note: Use a low box first and step down rather than jumping off to reduce impact.
